question: A right triangle with sides 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm is rotated about the sides of 3 cm to form a cone. The volume of the cone so formed is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When a right-angled triangle is rotated about one of its perpendicular sides, that side becomes the height of the generated cone.

Here, the triangle is rotated about the 3 cm side, so Height (h) = 3 cm.

The other perpendicular side becomes the base radius, so Radius (r) = 4 cm.

Volume of the cone = (1/3) × π × r² × h = (1/3) × π × 4² × 3 = 16π cm³.

**∴ The correct answer is 16π cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sides of the right-angled triangle = 3 cm, 4 cm, and 5 cm.

The triangle is rotated about the side of 3 cm.

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a cone = (1/3) × π × r² × h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d30669837d996ed67a375642589bfd3d4b10359bbba7df20cd05fadac6a2a1b7.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ When the triangle is rotated about the 3 cm side, this side becomes the axis of rotation.

⇒ Height of the cone (h) = 3 cm

⇒ Radius of the base (r) = 4 cm

⇒ Slant height (l) = Hypotenuse = 5 cm

⇒ Volume of the cone = (1/3) × π × (4)² × 3

⇒ Volume = (1/3) × π × 16 × 3

⇒ Volume = 16π cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 16π cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Rotation about the other side

If the same right triangle was rotated about the 4 cm side instead, the height would be 4 cm and the radius would be 3 cm. The resulting volume would be (1/3) × π × 3² × 4 = 12π cm³.

Rotation about the hypotenuse

If the triangle is rotated about its hypotenuse (5 cm), it forms a double cone. The common radius of these cones is given by (Base × Perpendicular) ÷ Hypotenuse = (3 × 4) ÷ 5 = 2.4 cm.

Surface Areas of a Cone

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = πrl and Total Surface Area (TSA) = πr(r + l), where r is the base radius and l is the slant height.
